findings: BRIEF 1 - 24-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge-utility-bill (definitive explainer; the page wins the cluster, draft supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity has canonical->this). Audience: bill-payers confused by the two buckets; deregulated shoppers sizing savings. Query/intent: 'delivery charge vs supply charge' - informational leading to a compare/shop decision. Missing vs need: one-utility (ConEd) sourcing, no per-utility split table, no 'can you shop it' answer, no regulated-vs-deregulated framing, no worked math; 424w refusal tone. Structure: Quick Answer with decision rule (delivery = wires/pipes + metering/billing, set by utility, not shoppable; supply = energy itself, shoppable in some states) -> two-bucket comparison table (covers | rate basis | who sets | shoppable?) -> verified per-utility split table, 3+ named utilities (supply rate, delivery components, share of total, where published) -> regulated vs deregulated states section -> worked 899-kWh month -> FAQ. Sources (fetch day 1, front-matter '(retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)'): ConEd how-to-read-your-bill (already cited); EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A, eia.gov/electricity/monthly/ (18.34c/kWh natl residential avg, Jun 2026, wave-1 verified); papowerswitch.com (PA PUC choice site); columbiagasohio.com Standard Choice Offer (gas-side supply auction); nationalgridus.com MA supply-costs page. Math: 899 kWh x 18.34c = $164.84 total, then split supply vs delivery using a named tariff's own published numbers - compute from fetched rates, never invent percentages. Visual: annotated sample bill color-coded supply lines vs delivery lines. Links out: 17-customer-charge, 18-fuel-adjustment, 49-demand-charges (demand is delivery-side), gas-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge; keep complete-guide mapping-table link; add hero_below_answer:true. Done bar: replaces absorbed draft's content, 3+-utility dated table with where-published column, worked split, FAQ schema, 4+ dated sources; target >=8/10 search-readiness on re-audit.

BRIEF 2 - duct-leaks-symptoms-hvac-running-all-day (intent realignment: title/slug/keywords promise symptoms + runtime; body refuses). Audience: homeowner with rooms uneven or HVAC running all day, deciding DIY checks vs pro test. Query/intent: 'duct leak symptoms', 'hvac running all day' - informational triage. Missing: zero named symptoms, no leakage statistic, no explanation of duct-blaster/blower-door testing, no sealing-material guidance. Structure: Quick Answer -> the promised symptom list (7-9, one-line cause each: uneven rooms, weak flow at far registers, dust streaks at joints/boots, runtime and bills climbing at same thermostat settings, stuffy rooms, visible kinks/torn flex in accessible attic, whistling returns) -> safe DIY observation checklist (registers, filter, visible return flex; no crawlspaces/improvements) -> what a professional measures (duct-blaster CFM25, blower door with ducts pressurized) -> sealing options (mastic/metal tape vs cloth duct tape) -> savings-claim guardrail (quote leakage % only as published) -> FAQ. Sources (dated '(retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)'): keep both DOE bsesc links (leakage-testing, high-R insulation); add ENERGY STAR heating/cooling maintenance page energystar.gov/campaign/heating_cooling and Energy Saver ducts page energy.gov/energysaver; quote ENERGY STAR's published leakage stat (commonly ~20-30% of conditioned air lost - verify exact wording, else omit). Math illustration, labeled as arithmetic not utility data: 15%/30% supply-side loss -> ~1.18x/~1.43x runtime to deliver same conditioned air, 3-row table. Visuals: annotated duct diagram with leak-point callouts; symptom-to-likely-cause table. Links out: heat-pump-running-all-day-in-winter (runtime sibling), 47-check-energy-leaks-home-diy; links in: heating-cooling-explained hub (wave-1 flagged missing), why-is-my-furnace-blowing-cold-air. Done bar: symptom list actually delivered and matches keywords, >=1 dated leakage source, runtime table, FAQ schema, ~900w.

BRIEF 3 - drought-surcharge-on-water-bill-explained (add the missing real rate table; today zero named utilities, zero dollars). Audience: water customer under a declared drought stage wondering why the bill jumped. Query/intent: 'drought surcharge water bill' - informational. Missing: no utility, no rates, no trigger stages, pure refusal posture. Structure: Quick Answer naming the 3 forms (fixed %-uplift on the bill; Stage-2+ tier-penalty/pivot rates; budget-based excess charges) -> verified example table, 2-3 utilities: declared stage/trigger, which tiers hit, % or $ uplift, where published -> worked before/after: 6 CCF (=4,488 gal, the site's own unit chain) bill under normal vs drought schedule on one named utility's published tiers, compute the $ delta -> drought charge vs excess-use fine vs ordinary tier creep (readers conflate all three) -> bill relief (leak adjustment is not drought relief; payment plans) -> FAQ. Sources (fetch day 1, date each '(retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)'; if a schedule expired, keep as labeled historical example): sanjosewater.com water-conservation/drought/drought-rate-information; marinwater.org drought surcharge schedule; austintexas.gov Austin Water conservation/drought rates; keep EPA WaterSense understanding-your-water-bill and EPA water-affordability pages. Visuals: drought-stage ladder infographic; before/after bill-line diagram. Links out: tiered-water-rates-explained, water-service-charge-explained, ccf-calculator, 44-how-to-lower-water-bill; links in: water-explained hub, 06-water-bill-too-high, why-is-my-water-bill-higher-in-summer. Done bar: >=1 dated named-utility table with dollar amounts + trigger stage, computed before/after delta, FAQ, hedges cut, ~900w; >=8/10 quality on re-audit.

BRIEF 4 - why-is-my-furnace-blowing-cold-air (keep safety spine verbatim; add the concrete checks and cost bands). Audience: homeowner in a cold snap with cool air from vents; YMYL-adjacent, CO safety is mandatory context. Query/intent: 'furnace blowing cold air' - urgent troubleshooting. Missing: causes never named (clogged filter -> limit-switch shutdown; condensate-clog lockout on 90%+ condensing furnaces; thermostat FAN ON instead of AUTO; ignition/pilot faults), no filter interval or size guidance, no cost context, no mention that 25C credits ended 12/31/2025 (verified - no rebate promises). Structure: Quick Answer (safety first, then check order) -> 15-minute check table (HEAT set above room temp; FAN AUTO not ON; filter inspect/replace; breaker + furnace switch; blocked exterior intake; CO alarm test) -> cause list with DIY-vs-call-pro column -> cost bands table (diagnostic visit, 1" filter prices, common repairs) dated to one fetchable cost source -> replacement reality with AFUE/lifespan from DOE -> keep CPSC stop-and-get-help block exactly as-is -> FAQ. Sources (dated '(retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)'): keep cpsc.gov CO Information Center + CPSC winter-storm release; add energystar.gov/campaign/heating_cooling (filter intervals), energy.gov/energysaver furnaces-and-boilers (AFUE, lifespan), one verified cost source (Angi or HomeGuide furnace-repair page - writer fetches and dates; if unavailable, no dollar bands). Visuals: thermostat AUTO-vs-FAN-ON annotated graphic; filter decision table. Links out: duct-leaks post, aux-heat-vs-emergency-heat-meaning, 13-ac-short-cycling-causes-fixes, 48-heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings; links in: heating-cooling hub, 13. Done bar: >=3 concrete figures in the checks, dated cost table, safety block unchanged, FAQ, ~1,000w.

Front matter: convert the 3 bare DOE PDF URLs to titled + '(retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)' convention; add hero_below_answer:true. Sources: keep 3 DOE bill guides; add EIA EPM eia.gov/electricity/monthly/, EIA gas price table, Austin Energy residential line items page (real worked-bill anchor already verified in exemplar #17), EPA WaterSense. Links in: homepage Essential-guides, utility-bills-costs-explained hub (wave-1 flagged adding an explicit funnel there), 03-why-is-my-electric-bill-so-high, 04-hidden-fees; keep all charge-map links out. Done bar: title/slug/keywords aligned; a first-time reader maps every line of their own bill to a linked explainer without leaving the 5 steps; >=1 verified-dollar worked breakdown; >=2 visuals incl. annotated bill; FAQ schema live; >=8/10 both scores at re-audit.
